answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by staking reputation in a trust kernel: every identity must lock real, costly compute or attestable history before it can transact. Like a dam holding back the timber tide, this makes flooding the market with fake identities prohibitively expensive. New agents start with narrow, low-trust permissions and earn broader access only through verified, peer-attested work. Since sybils can't fake the kernel of accumulated trust, their numbers stop mattering.
